title: Cup-product transpose detects the evaluation counit
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be flat, proper and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and suppose the unit $\mathcal O_T\to p_*p^*\mathcal O_T$ of the tensor-pullback adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] is invertible after every base change $T\to S$. Let $E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Let $j:W\to S$ satisfy $P(f,E,hj)$ for every $h:T\to W$ [def-sc-picard-direct-image-rank-condition]. Put $p:X_W\to W$, $q:X_W\to X$, $N=p_*q^*E$ and $D=p_*q^*(E^\vee)$, where $E^\vee=\mathcal Hom(E,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Then $D$ is finite locally free and there is a morphism $\varphi:D\to N^\vee$ such that, for every $h:T\to W$, $h^*\varphi$ is invertible if and only if the canonical counit $p_T^*p_{T*}q_T^*E\to q_T^*E$ is invertible.

proof.text: Apply the universal rank condition to identity morphisms on W. Around each point it gives simultaneous rank-r trivializations for N, D and the pulled-back E. Consequently D is finite locally free and N is finite locally free by the explicit first conjunct.

Identify q^*(E^dual) with (q^*E)^dual by the finite free dual basis calculation. Define the pairing N tensor D to O_W by pushforward of evaluation and the inverse of O_W to p_*O_{X_W}. The latter is obtained from hO and the pullback structure-sheaf isomorphism. Transposing gives phi:D to N^dual. Naturality of these maps and the canonical base-change isomorphisms in the rank condition identify h^*phi with the cup-product transpose for every test scheme. Iterated pullbacks are compared by the canonical composition isomorphisms.

An invertible transpose gives local dual bases sigma_i and tau_j with products delta_ij. Viewed upstairs, sigma_i define exactly the adjunction counit and tau_j define its left inverse. Source and target are locally free of the same rank r. A left inverse for a square matrix makes its determinant a unit; the adjugate then gives a two-sided inverse. Thus the counit is invertible. Conversely an invertible counit identifies E_T with p_T^*N_T. Dualization and the finite locally free projection formula identify D_T with N_T^dual tensor p_{T*}O_{X_T}, hence N_T^dual. The pairing is evaluation under this identification, so its transpose is invertible. Both arguments apply to arbitrary rings; when r=0 both maps are isomorphisms of zero modules, and the empty base is vacuous.

theorem exists_picardCupProductCriterion {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hO : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S),
      IsIso ((Classical.choose
        (Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (pullback.snd f g))).unit.app
          (SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf)))
    (E : X.Modules) [E.IsFiniteLocallyFree]
    {W : Scheme.{u}} (j : W ⟶ S)
    (hW : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (h : T ⟶ W), PicardDirectImageRankCondition f E (h ≫ j)) :
    ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd f j)).obj
      ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f j)).obj (Modules.dual E))).IsFiniteLocallyFree ∧
    ∃ φ : ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd f j)).obj
        ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f j)).obj (Modules.dual E))) ⟶
      Modules.dual ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd f j)).obj
        ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f j)).obj E)),
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (h : T ⟶ W),
        IsIso ((Modules.tensorPullback h).map φ) ↔
          IsIso ((Classical.choose
            (Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (pullback.snd f (h ≫ j)))).counit.app
              ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f (h ≫ j))).obj E))
